texts.facts: Petitioners are accused Nos.4 and 3 in S.T.No.533 of 2019 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Ranni. The case originated from a complaint filed by the Food Safety Officer alleging that, on 07.01.2017, 48 bottles of Lehar Evervess Club Soda was being offered for sale by the vendor in Stall No.77, Sabari Hotel, Hill Top, Pamba. Out of the 48 bottles, 8 bottles were taken as samples from the 1st accused and on being subjected to analysis was found not to be in conformity with prescribed standards. Accordingly, a complaint was launched by arraying the vendor as the 1st accused, the Distributor as the 2nd accused, the Manufacturer as the 4th accused and its Nominee as the 3rd accused. This Crl.M.C is filed seeking to quash the proceedings against the 2025:KER:18041 petitioners on the ground that, by the time sample bottles were taken and subjected to analysis, the shelf life, ie., the period of nine months from manufacturing, was over.
texts.arguments: 2. Learned Counsel for the petitioners pointed out that the samples were taken up on 07.01.2017 and the manufacturing date being 27.02.2016, the 9 months was over by 26.11.2016. Thereafter, the reference was made to Annexure-B report of the Food Analyst to point out that the analysis was Pepsico India Holdings Private Limited vs The State Of Kerala on 17 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44793701/ 2 done on 25.01.2017. It is the further submission of the learned Counsel that the notice for re-analysis under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act was given to the Manufacturer only on 02.08.2017, rendering the entire process of futile exercise. It is contended that insofar as the shelf life of the article had expired, the 2025:KER:18041 Manufacturer cannot be mulcted with any liability since going by Section 27(2) and (3), liability is that of the wholesaler, distributor or the seller 3. I heard the learned ADGP also. A reading of Section 27(2) of the FSS Act, is to the effect that the wholesaler or distributor shall be liable under 2025:KER:18041 the Act for any article or food which is supplied after the date of its expiry. Similarly, Section 27(3)(a) stipulates that the seller shall be liable under this Act for any article or food which is sold after the date of its expiry.
